answer: At most 5 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a pearl tag. The quartz cap is policed at intake and mesa makes public the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool therefore cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch whatever the capital it holds, since every participant consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 12 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
